correctness.rationale: The final claim is for every complex harmonic f:D→closed D with |f(0)|=a and the two-sided Fourier majorant. Reconstructed L∞ Poisson boundary trace and Parseval: sum over n≠0 |c_n|²≤1−a². Cauchy–Schwarz against weights r^|n| yields B_f(r)−a≤sqrt(2(1−a²))r/sqrt(1−r²), equivalent to admissible r²≤(1−a)/(3+a). Independent Taylor integration of the explicit unimodular even trace exp(i ε cos θ) gives c_0=1−ε²/4+O(ε⁴) and c_{1}=c_{−1}=i ε/2+O(ε³). The first harmonic alone violates the majorant above r=(1−a)/(ε+O(ε³))=(1/2+o(1))sqrt(1−a). The mean is strictly decreasing for small ε>0 so witnesses every nearby a. Harmonic maximum principle at a=1 forces f constant and R_H(1)=1. Hence exact sharp endpoint law but no claim of globally exact R_H(a) for interior a.
